prompt: A male lion faces the camera in the golden grass of the Serengeti at late afternoon, his full mane cascading in thick waves of dark brown and amber from the crown of his head to his broad chest. His wide-set amber eyes are calm and direct, nostrils relaxed, and the bridge of his nose is smooth and unscarred. The savanna behind him is equally sharp—every blade of dry golden grass, a single flat-topped acacia tree on the horizon, and the pale blue sky with a band of warm cloud are all in the same unforgiving focus as the individual hairs of his mane and the coarse fur across his muzzle.

A Bengal tiger stands chest-deep in a mangrove creek in the Sundarbans, its face turned directly toward the camera, water dripping from its chin and whiskers. The orange-and-black striped face, the white ruff beneath the jaw, and the pale green eyes are rendered with the same sharpness as the dark tannic water, the aerial roots of the mangroves on both banks, and the dense green canopy stretching overhead. The light is overcast and even, eliminating harsh shadows and giving the tiger's wet fur a rich, saturated glow against the muted green-brown of the swamp.

A snow leopard crouches on a granite ledge in the Karakoram range, its pale grey-green eyes staring forward, the spotted face framed by thick cheek ruffs of smoke-grey fur. Every rosette on the face, every whisker, and every crack in the lichen-covered rock beneath its chin is uniformly sharp, and the vast Himalayan landscape behind—snow-dusted ridges, a glacial valley, and distant peaks against a cold blue sky—is rendered with identical clarity. The light is the flat, cool brightness of a high-altitude winter morning.

A bald eagle perches on a dead spruce snag at the edge of an Alaskan river, its white-feathered head turned slightly, the hooked yellow beak and the fierce pale eye facing the camera. The eagle's head feathers, the bark texture of the snag, the rushing grey-green river below, and the snow-covered Chugach Mountains on the far bank are all in equal focus. The light is overcast and silver, the eagle's white head the brightest element against the dark spruce forest lining both riverbanks.

A silverback mountain gorilla sits in a clearing of montane bamboo forest in the Virunga Mountains, his broad black face turned forward, the deep-set brown eyes calm beneath the prominent sagittal crest. His flared nostrils, the grey-salted hair on his brow, and the massive jaw are in the same sharp detail as the bamboo stalks behind him, the volcanic soil at his feet, and the misty green slopes of the volcano rising above the canopy. The light is diffused through cloud, rendering the gorilla's black fur and the green forest in rich, even tones.

A grey wolf stands on a lichen-covered rock in the Yellowstone backcountry, its golden eyes locked on the camera, ears pricked forward, muzzle slightly lowered. The wolf's grizzled grey-and-cream face, the guard hairs backlit by the low sun, and the individual whiskers are as sharp as the rock's orange lichen, the sage-covered valley below, and the distant Absaroka Range under a sky of pale blue and thin cloud. The autumn light is horizontal and warm, catching the wolf's fur in a golden rim while the landscape stretches in equal clarity behind.

A polar bear stands on a slab of sea ice in Hudson Bay, its massive cream-white head facing the camera, black nose and dark eyes the only contrast in the pale face. The coarse fur, the small rounded ears, and the broad muzzle are in the same sharp focus as the cracked and ridged ice surface, the dark lead of open water behind, and the flat white horizon where ice meets an overcast sky. The light is the flat, blue-white of an Arctic autumn, and the bear's fur carries a faint yellow warmth against the cool monochrome of the ice field.

A red fox sits in a snow-covered meadow at the edge of a birch forest in Hokkaido, its sharp orange face pointed directly at the camera, black-tipped ears erect, amber eyes bright. The fox's whiskers, the snow crystals on its muzzle, and the individual guard hairs are rendered with the same sharpness as the white birch trunks behind, the undisturbed snow stretching to the treeline, and the heavy grey sky above. The light is flat winter overcast, and the fox's vivid orange coat is the only warm colour in a landscape of white, grey, and pale bark.

An African elephant stands at the edge of a waterhole in Amboseli at golden hour, its massive grey face filling the left half of the frame, the wrinkled skin, the small amber eye, and the curve of a tusk in sharp detail. The waterhole's muddy red shore, the reflections of the surrounding acacias in the still water, and the enormous snow-capped dome of Kilimanjaro rising behind are all rendered with identical sharpness. The low sun paints the elephant's skin warm and gilds the mountain's glaciers, and the scale between the animal's textured hide and the distant peak reads clearly across the entire frame.

A great horned owl perches on the limb of a ponderosa pine in a Montana canyon at dusk, its ear tufts erect, enormous yellow eyes staring directly forward, the barred breast plumage sharp against the rough bark. The pine's orange bark plates, the canyon's layered sandstone walls, and the pale evening sky with the first visible planet are all in equal focus. The light is the last ambient glow before nightfall—cool and even, the owl's yellow eyes the most luminous element in a landscape fading from warm ochre to cool blue-grey.

A green sea turtle rests on a coral ledge in the Red Sea, its ancient face turned toward the camera, the beak-like mouth closed, the dark eye calm and unhurried. The scutes of its shell, the algae growth on the shell's ridges, the branching coral beneath, and the blue water column stretching upward to a rippled surface of sunlight are all uniformly in focus. The underwater light is clear and directional, casting the turtle's shadow on the coral and illuminating the individual polyps and the small reef fish hovering at the ledge's edge.

A jaguar lies on the exposed root system of a ceiba tree at the edge of a Pantanal river, its spotted face resting on crossed forepaws, green-gold eyes half-open and watching. The rosette pattern on the face, the massive jaw, and the short tawny fur are in the same sharp detail as the ceiba's buttress roots, the dark slow-moving river behind, the floating water hyacinths, and the gallery forest on the far bank. The light is hot and midday, filtered through the canopy in bright patches that fall equally on the cat and the tangled vegetation.

A harpy eagle perches on a kapok tree branch in the Amazonian canopy, its grey-and-white face framed by a raised crest of dark feathers, the massive hooked beak and piercing grey eyes facing the camera. The feather barbs, the branch's epiphyte-covered bark, the surrounding canopy of broad leaves, and a distant gap revealing the river far below are all uniformly sharp. The light is the bright, diffused green of a tropical midday filtered through the upper canopy, and the eagle's pale chest and dark back create a stark tonal contrast against the uniform green.

A Galápagos marine iguana sits on black lava rock above the Pacific surf, its blunt snout and salt-crusted face turned toward the camera, the dark scales and the red-and-green algae colouring on its head vivid against the volcanic stone. The iguana's conical head scales, the rough aa lava texture, the white salt spray on the rocks, and the turquoise ocean stretching to the horizon are all in equal focus. The equatorial sun is high and direct, casting short shadows that define every scale and every bubble in the lava's vesicular surface.

A snowy owl sits on a fence post in a Manitoba prairie in winter, its round white face and bright yellow eyes facing the camera, the dark barring on its plumage sharp against the snow-covered field behind. Every feather barb, every weathered grain in the wooden post, the barbed-wire fence receding to a vanishing point, and the flat white horizon are uniformly in focus. The light is pale and cold, the sky a featureless white that merges with the snow, and the owl's yellow eyes are the warmest colour in the entire frame.

A Komodo dragon lies on a sun-baked hillside on Rinca Island, its heavy head resting on the ground, the forked yellow tongue partially extended, the dark beady eyes staring directly at the camera. The pebbly scales of its face, the loose dewlap skin, the dry grass and volcanic rock beneath, and the turquoise Flores Sea and the distant island silhouettes on the horizon are all in the same sharp focus. The midday tropical sun is harsh and overhead, casting the dragon's body shadow tight beneath it and rendering every scale in high contrast.

A mandrill sits on a fallen mahogany log in a Cameroon rainforest, its extraordinary face turned toward the camera—the blue-ridged nose, the scarlet nostrils, the golden beard, and the close-set amber eyes all rendered in vivid, sharp detail. The log's bark texture, the forest floor's leaf litter, the massive buttress roots of surrounding trees, and the green canopy filtering light far above are all equally in focus. The light is a patchwork of bright sun and deep shade, the mandrill's pigmented face catching a shaft of direct light while the forest stretches behind in intricate, uniformly detailed layers of green and brown.

A grey whale surfaces in a Baja California lagoon, its barnacle-encrusted head breaking the calm water, the blowhole open, one dark eye visible just above the waterline. The barnacles, the callosities, and the mottled grey skin are in the same sharp detail as the water's surface texture, the desert hills of the Vizcaíno coast in the middle distance, and the pale blue sky above. The light is bright and clear, the whale's wet skin catching the sun in a broad highlight, and the lagoon's green-brown water is shallow enough to show the sandy bottom in the foreground.

A resplendent quetzal perches on a moss-covered branch in a Costa Rican cloud forest, its iridescent green head and red breast facing the camera, the long emerald tail streamers hanging below the branch. Every barb of the metallic green head feathers, the crimson breast plumage, the moss and orchid growth on the branch, and the misty cloud forest stretching behind in layers of dark green trunks and hanging epiphytes are all uniformly sharp. The cloud forest light is soft and diffused, the quetzal's iridescent feathers shifting between green and gold depending on the angle of each barb.

An Arctic fox in its white winter coat sits on a snow-covered tundra ridge in Svalbard, its small face turned directly to the camera, dark eyes and black nose the only contrast against the white fur and the white landscape. The fox's dense underfur, the wind-sculpted snow drifts on the ridge, the frozen fjord in the valley below, and the distant glaciated mountains under a pale pink-and-blue Arctic twilight sky are all in equal focus. The light is the low, long glow of polar twilight, painting the snow in faint tones of lavender and peach, and the fox's white coat picks up every subtle colour shift in the sky.
